subject: Subprocessor inventory & DPA amendment for HearthTech integration
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@hearthtech.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@hearthtech.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor inventory & DPA amendment for HearthTech integration

Hi Naomi,

Hope you're well — HearthTech is moving towards a production integration with Redwood and our legal/compliance team has asked for a couple of items before we can finalize the contract:

1) A current subprocessor roster (name, country of operation, processing purpose, and whether they have access to logs or identifiable PII).
2) Evidence items: SOC 2 attestation link (or certificate), confirmation of KMS/HSM usage for customer key material, and any residency constraints per processor.
3) A short dataflow diagram or summary describing cross-border transfers and any caching or telemetry relays that might route data outside of the US.

We have a compliance cutoff of Sept 24 to complete our vendor review. If possible, can you send the roster and a draft DPA addendum that captures the residency/KMS commitments by EOD Monday (Sept 21 PT)? If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute call to walk through specifics — Tom (cc'd) is our security lead and will join.

Thanks — Alyssa

--
Alyssa Chen
Head of Integrations | HearthTech
alyssa.chen@hearthtech.com
+1 (415) 555-0119
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor inventory & DPA amendment for HearthTech integration

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the note and the timeline. We're happy to prioritize this. Attached are two documents to start: a current subprocessor roster and a concise dataflow summary. The roster includes country, processing purpose, and whether the processor handles logs or identifies tokens.

Quick summary:
- All primary inference and KV cache processors are US-based; we do have an analytics relay vendor that occasionally routes telemetry through EU points for aggregation (no customer prompt content).
- Customer key material is encrypted at rest; we support KMS integrations and use HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/private deployments.
- SOC 2 Type II report is hosted via our compliance portal — I can share a one-time access link once you confirm who should receive it.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20260918.csv, dataflow-summary_hearthtech.pdf

Would Wed 20 Sep 10:00 AM PT work for a quick review call? Grace (CSM) will join to cover onboarding, and Marcus (infra) can address any technical key/residency questions.

Naomi
Director, Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@hearthtech.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA addendum for HearthTech — request for confirmation

Hi Alyssa / Naomi,

Following Naomi's materials, I've put together a short draft DPA addendum that captures: explicit subprocessor list inclusion, a clause on KMS/HSM usage and key residency options, and a paragraph listing fallback routing policies (onshore-only option for US customers).

Please review the attached: dpa_addendum_hearthtech_draft.docx. A couple of points for confirmation from HearthTech:
- Do you require Redwood to guarantee onshore-only (US) transit for all prompts, or is onshore-at-rest sufficient?
- The analytics relay we noted in the roster: please confirm whether you need that vendor excluded entirely from any cross-border transfers (we can document an exclusion).

If those items look OK, I can prepare a DocuSign package for signature. I have a DocuSign template ready here: https://app.docusign.com/templates/abcd-1234.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@hearthtech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@hearthtech.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA addendum for HearthTech — request for confirmation

Kimberly / Naomi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few quick confirmations:

1) Onshore transit: HearthTech requires onshore-only transit for any request payloads that contain customer PII or payment data. Non-PII telemetry may be routed for aggregation, but we'd prefer analytics_relay be excluded from EU transfers for our account.
2) KMS: We will provide our own customer-managed key for encrypting stored customer data; please confirm Redwood can accept an external KMS key (we use AWS KMS with an external key policy).

If you can incorporate the analytics_relay exclusion and an explicit clause that Redwood will accept provided external KMS keys (and indicate any restrictions), we can sign the addendum. I've attached our PO for procurement reference (HT-PO-4432.pdf).

On Wed's call we'll reconfirm the cutover plan. Looking forward to the DocuSign link once the edits are in place.

Best,
Alyssa
--

Head of Integrations | HearthTech
